content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions, adverse effects, and monitoring recommendations for itraconazole when co-administered with various medications. Itraconazole can alter the metabolism of drugs by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to increased drug levels or effects. This interaction is clinically significant in many cases and requires careful monitoring or alternative therapy. 1. Topotecan: Itraconazole increases topotecan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Concomitant use with oral topotecan is not recommended due to significant interaction risks. For IV topotecan, the interaction may be less severe but still clinically relevant. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Toremifene: Itraconazole increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. 3. Trametinib: Itraconazole increases trametinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Trazodone: Trazodone reduces itraconazole levels via P-glycoprotein induction, while itraconazole increases trazodone levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. 5. Triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension: Itraconazole increases triamcinolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 6. Triazolam: Itraconazole significantly increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 7. Triclabendazole: Both itraconazole and triclabendazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Trifluoperazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 9. Trimethoprim: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 10. Trimipramine: Itraconazole increases trimipramine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 11. Triptorelin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tropisetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 13. Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid concomitant use. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as per product labeling. 14. Ubrogepant: Itraconazole increases ubrogepant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 15. Ulipristal: Itraconazole increases ulipristal levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled: Itraconazole increases systemic exposure to these drugs, which are CYP3A4 substrates. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 17. Upadacitinib: Itraconazole increases upadacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Valbenazine: Itraconazole increases valbenazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 19. Vamorolone: Itraconazole increases vamorolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone and monitor closely. 20. Vandetanib: Itraconazole increases vandetanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 21. Vardenafil: Itraconazole increases vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 22. Velpatasvir: Itraconazole increases velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Vemurafenib: Itraconazole increases vemurafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 24. Venetoclax: Itraconazole increases venetoclax levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Concomitant use is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up phase. After this phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75% if co-administered. 25. Venlafaxine: Itraconazole increases venlafaxine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Verapamil: Itraconazole increases verapamil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs have additive negative inotropic effects. Avoid or use alternative therapy. Monitor for signs of verapamil toxicity, such as peripheral edema, dizziness, hypotension, and headache. 27. Vilazodone: Itraconazole increases vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily if co-administered. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 28. Vinblastine: Itraconazole increases vinblastine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Vincristine: Itraconazole increases vincristine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Vincristine liposomal: Itraconazole increases vincristine liposomal levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Vinorelbine: Itraconazole increases vinorelbine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Voclosporin: Itraconazole increases voclosporin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval and may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 33. Vonoprazan: Vonoprazan reduces itraconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after vonoprazan. 34. Vorapaxar: Itraconazole increases vorapaxar levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 35. Voriconazole: Itraconazole increases voriconazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 36. Vorinostat: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Voxilaprevir: Itraconazole increases voxilaprevir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Warfarin: Itraconazole increases warfarin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism of the R-enantiomer. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 39. Zafirlukast: Zafirlukast increases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 40. Zaleplon: Itraconazole increases zaleplon levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Zanubrutinib: Itraconazole increases zanubrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg daily if co-administered. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing itraconazole. 42. Ziprasidone: Itraconazole increases ziprasidone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative therapy. 43. Zolpidem: Itraconazole increases zolpidem levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Zonisamide: Itraconazole increases zonisamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Zuranolone: Itraconazole increases zuranolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the zuranolone dose if co-administered. Adverse Effects: Itraconazole is associated with a range of adverse effects, including but not limited to rash, vomiting, edema, headache, abnormal liver function tests, diarrhea, fatigue, hypertension, pruritus, abdominal pain, dizziness, hypertriglyceridemia, hypokalemia, anorexia, somnolence, and impotence. Serious adverse effects include hepatotoxicity, cardiac failure, and QT prolongation. Close monitoring is essential when itraconazole is used, especially in combination with other medications.
